A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffusion of Li+ ions in the LiNiO2 lattice is fast and that the diffusion of vacancies in this lattice is even faster.
the diffusion of Li+ ions in LiNiO2 occurs by a vacancy mechanism, with a diffusion coefficient which is amongst the largest observed for a lithium containing solid.

the diffusion coefficient is enhanced by the presence of lithium vacancies and that the thermodynamics of the lithium intercalation reaction is also strongly influenced by the presence of these vacancies.

the rate of lithium diffusion is very high in LiNiO2.
the rate of lithium transport in the intercalant is not limited by the rate of lithium diffusion, but rather the rate of lithium insertion and removal.
the diffusion coefficients of the lithium ions in this compound are much larger than in other intercalation compounds.
